resources.string: Stop Facebook photos from flooding Google Photos

On Xiaomi devices, Facebook saves photos and videos into DCIM/Facebook, which is inside your camera roll. Google Photos treats that folder as part of your camera roll and backs everything up -- often within seconds.
This app watches that folder in real time and moves each new file into a separate Facebook_Saved folder within milliseconds of it being written, deleting the original from DCIM/Facebook before Google Photos gets a chance to sync it. A small persistent notification keeps this watcher alive; a 15-minute backup check also runs in case the watcher ever gets restarted by the system.
To do this it needs \"All files access\" — without it, Android blocks apps from deleting files they didn\'t create themselves, which is the \"permission denied\" error you may have hit before.
✅ All files access granted. Real-time watcher is active, plus a 15-minute backup sweep.
⚠️ All files access not granted yet. Nothing can be moved or deleted without it.
Disable Battery Optimization For This App

Xiaomi\'s MIUI/HyperOS aggressively kills background apps and services even when permissions are granted. For the watcher to survive, also do this once:
1. Security app → App Battery Saver → find this app → set to \"No restrictions\". 2. Security app → Permissions → Autostart → enable Autostart for this app. 3. Recent apps screen → swipe this app\'s card down (or tap the lock icon) to lock it so MIUI doesn\'t sweep it away.
The button below opens the Security app\'s permissions screen where most of this lives; the exact menu wording varies by MIUI version.
Source: /storage/emulated/0/DCIM/Facebook/ Destination: /storage/emulated/0/Facebook_Saved/ Real-time watcher: instant (FileObserver) Backup sweep: every 15 minutes
Keeps this app alive to instantly move Facebook photos out of your camera roll.
